n: Crowdfunding and Social Media Fundraising for Terrorist Financing
ds: Online fundraising platforms, social media appeals and messaging channels can be used to solicit small donations across many jurisdictions for violent groups, often presenting as humanitarian or community causes. Detection combines campaign content intelligence with payment patterns across payment processors, banks and platforms.

src.t: FATF, Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment Guidance (2019)

cn.rt: Donations to crowdfunding or social media appeals paid and received by everyday accounts via remote channels.

rat: Online fundraising with many small donations via platforms and wallets.

ind.n: Campaign narrative linked to extremist content or designated groups
ind.cx: Fundraising page, post or channel references violent groups, glorifies violence or is linked to accounts removed for extremism.
ind.fp: Political or religious speech, and news reporting, may reference the same topics lawfully.
ind.ds: Fundraising page, post or channel references violent groups, glorifies violence or is linked to accounts removed for extremism.

ind.n: Many small donations from geographically diverse donors to a single organiser
ind.cx: Large numbers of low-value contributions from many countries into one recipient account that then withdraws promptly.
ind.fp: Viral humanitarian appeals and memorial funds show similar patterns.
ind.ds: Large numbers of low-value contributions from many countries into one recipient account that then withdraws promptly.

ind.n: Payout to account unrelated to organiser or declared beneficiary
ind.cx: Funds are paid to third-party accounts, prepaid cards or wallets that do not match the organiser's verified identity.
ind.fp: Campaigns for medical treatment are often paid to relatives or institutions.
ind.ds: Payouts or disbursements are directed to bank accounts, cards or wallets that do not match the verified customer or declared beneficiary.
ind.cn: Payout to account not matching verified identity or declared beneficiary

ind.n: Use of coded language, rapid channel migration or deleted campaigns
ind.cx: Organiser moves between platforms or handles, closes campaigns and restarts under new names after scrutiny.
ind.fp: Privacy-conscious users and harassment victims also change handles.
ind.ds: Organiser moves between platforms or handles, closes campaigns and restarts under new names after scrutiny.

ind.n: Donations routed to cryptocurrency addresses or messaging-app collection points
ind.cx: Appeal asks for crypto transfers or direct contact on encrypted channels instead of regulated payment methods.
ind.fp: Crypto donations are legitimate in some communities.
ind.ds: Appeal asks for crypto transfers or direct contact on encrypted channels instead of regulated payment methods.

ind.n: Campaigns exploiting a crisis event with unverified beneficiaries
ind.cx: Appeals created immediately after conflict or disaster events with no known organisation behind them and no verifiable delivery route.
ind.fp: Genuine rapid-response efforts frequently emerge informally.
ind.ds: Appeals created immediately after conflict or disaster events with no known organisation behind them and no verifiable delivery route.

ind.n: Funds withdrawn as cash or via ATM in higher-risk border regions
ind.cx: Collected funds are cashed out near conflict zones or high-risk borders shortly after payout.
ind.fp: Residents and aid workers also transact in those regions.
ind.ds: Cash withdrawals, ATM or card use occur at transit points or border regions near conflict zones.
ind.cn: Cash or card use in border and transit areas near conflict zones

ind.cx: Organiser identity documents, contact details or IP geolocation do not align with claimed location or purpose.
ind.fp: VPN use and travel create geolocation mismatches.
ind.ds: Identity documents, contact details, geolocation or device data do not align, suggesting fabricated, stolen or misrepresented identity.
ind.cn: Inconsistent or synthetic identity data at onboarding

ctl.ds: Participates in sector, regulator and public-private forums and platform cooperation to receive and share typologies and indicators where lawful. It keeps scenarios current.

ctl.n: Seller, organiser and payee verification with payout controls
ctl.ds: Verifies sellers, workers and fundraising organisers, matches payees to verified identities and holds or staggers payouts for new or anomalous accounts. It limits platform abuse.
Monitors for spoofed domains, fake apps, adverts, numbers and fraudulent campaigns, and arranges takedown, suspension and customer alerts. It removes criminal infrastructure.

ctl.n: Fan-in, fan-out and funnel account detection
ctl.ds: Detects accounts receiving from many unrelated senders, or sending to many beneficiaries, followed by consolidation or onward movement. It surfaces collector, funnel and mule structures.

ctl.n: Account detail change monitoring and cool-down
ctl.ds: Contact, device or payee changes trigger notification to the prior channel and restrict risky actions for a short period, with alerts on clusters of changes. It disrupts takeover.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.

ctl.n: Duplicate and synthetic identity checks at onboarding
ctl.ds: Compares new applicant identifiers such as name, email, phone, address, device and bank account with existing customers, previously declined or exited applicants and known-bad data. Matches are blocked or referred, limiting repeat applicants, synthetic identities and mule recruitment.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.
Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.
Sets internal risk guidance, acceptance limits and approval levels for sectors, commodities and fundraising channels exposed to elevated risk. It gives consistent decisions on how far to engage.

Provides targeted messaging that helps customers recognise scam scripts and mule recruitment, verify requests independently and use trusted routes for giving or paying. It reduces victimisation and unwitting participation.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

Caps transaction size, frequency, load, withdrawal and deposit values, with staged increases as legitimate behaviour is established and per-customer limits at kiosks. It bounds the loss and laundering capacity of new or higher-risk accounts.

Remote verification of a person's identity using document capture, biometric matching and liveness or anti-spoofing checks, or a trusted digital identity. It reduces impersonation, synthetic identities and account opening with stolen or fabricated credentials.

Detects use of VPN, proxy and anonymising services and compares access geolocation with declared residence and sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions. It reveals concealed location and supports geographic restrictions.
